title: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.01728v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) tackle challenging tasks by dividing work among agents and coordinating their contributions toward shared objectives. Evaluating these systems therefore requires benchmarks that assess not only task-solving performance but also the ability to handle interdependent work. However, existing benchmarks often emphasize task difficulty without substantial collaboration requirements or evaluate only a limited range of predefined collaboration patterns. In this paper, we introduce MAC-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaboration through interconnected tasks. Rather than imposing predefined agent roles or communication protocols, MAC-Bench embeds collaboration requirements directly into task dependencies and shared-resource constraints. translated_title: MAC-Bench：通过互联任务对多智能体协作进行基准测试
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的多智能体系统（MAS）通过在智能体之间分配工作，并协调各自的贡献以实现共同目标，从而解决具有挑战性的任务。因此，评估这些系统需要这样的基准：不仅要评估任务求解性能，还要评估处理相互依赖工作的能力。然而，现有的基准往往强调任务难度但缺乏实质性的协作需求，或者仅评估有限的预定义协作模式。在本文中，我们提出了MAC-Bench，这是一个通过互联任务全面评估多智能体协作能力的基准。MAC-Bench并不强制规定预定义的智能体角色或通信协议，而是将协作需求直接嵌入到任务依赖关系和共享资源约束之中。具体而言，我们在两个层面上从选定的基准任务中挖掘可复用的协作结构。局部协作模式……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出MAC-Bench基准，通过将协作需求直接嵌入任务依赖关系和共享资源约束中，而非强加预定义的智能体角色或通信协议，来全面评估基于大语言模型的多智能体系统的协作能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MAC-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates multi-agent collaboration by embedding collaboration requirements directly into task dependencies and shared-resource constraints, rather than imposing predefined agent roles or communication protocols.
